# HSparkline

> A small SVG trend with a textual summary, finite-data handling, and semantic tones.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This describes repository source for version 0.4.0. Match documentation to your installed source/release.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HSparkline` from `@hearth-ui/vue`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-sparkline>`.
- Constructor: `HearthSparklineElement` from `@hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Surfaces.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HSparkline.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- A small trend, not a full charting/analytics engine. Supply a short, aggregated numeric series and a meaningful label or description.
- Non-finite values are ignored; flat, single-value, and empty series have explicit rendering behavior. Set decorative only when adjacent content supplies equivalent information.

## Public API

values: number[] · label, description: string · tone: Tone · width, height: number · decorative: boolean

A `?` marks optional source props. Props with defaults may be omitted. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    values: number[];
    label: string;
    description?: string;
    tone?: Tone;
    width?: number;
    height?: number;
    decorative?: boolean;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{ values: () => [], tone: "accent", width: 160, height: 48 }
```

### Events

None

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose argument arrays in `event.detail`. Listen on the element. Native events such as `click` retain their normal payloads. The elements package provides framework-independent DOM event types.

### Slots

None

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Web components do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base

Use `hearth-sparkline::part(part-name)` for an exposed part or inherited `--h-*` tokens for shared styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Supporting types

```ts
export type Tone = "neutral" | "accent" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "info";
```

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { HSparkline } from '@hearth-ui/vue';
import '@hearth-ui/vue/styles.css';

</script>

<template>
  <HSparkline :values="[3,5,4,8,6,9]" label="Requests over six samples" tone="info" />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point. For field submission, use an owning native form; the auth page already contains its own form.

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

This is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Initial array/object properties are assigned before connection to establish reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@hearth-ui/elements';
import '@hearth-ui/elements/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-sparkline');
Object.assign(element, {
  "values": [
    3,
    5,
    4,
    8,
    6,
    9
  ],
  "label": "Requests over six samples",
  "tone": "info"
});

mount.append(element);
```
